source: Hallmarks and Growth States, 11 Oct 2026 (story_v2 Step 13); Lee et al. 2018 PNAS 115:4471; Hubert et al. 2024 Nat Commun 15:6161

hallmarks.hallmark: Cells arrive and land; the flow decides where and how many
hallmarks.partaker: Cells on the glass over time sit on Lee et al.'s curve (their Fig. 2B)

hallmarks.hallmark: Most cells leave again within seconds (reversible attachment)
hallmarks.partaker: 96.9 % of landings leave within 30 s, theirs 96.7 %

hallmarks.hallmark: A cell standing on its end can still leave; a cell lying flat settles (pose)
hallmarks.partaker: Flat landings stay far more often (13 % against under 1 %); no published number

hallmarks.hallmark: Stronger flow: fewer cells land, but those that land stay longer
Cells crawl on the glass; committed cells go still
hallmarks.partaker: Flow cell 1 matches; the stillness of flow cell 2 is not reproduced

hallmarks.hallmark: After a division one daughter often leaves; later both stay
hallmarks.partaker: Wild type and pilA match; pilU's shift not reproduced

hallmarks.hallmark: Cells that met a surface stick sooner (memory)
hallmarks.partaker: All seven lag times within 0.24 h

hallmarks.hallmark: Under flow some cells stop dividing and hold on; the colony grows slower
hallmarks.partaker: Growth rate matches at 7 and 72 per s and the share of holders under gentle flow; strong flow not reproduced

hallmarks.hallmark: Only some landed cells switch on the biofilm programme
Early cells leave sugar trails that steer the next ones
